newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fischer seeks "more accurate value" for A$.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fischer seeks "more accurate value" for A$.

text.p: Australia's deputy prime minister, Tim Fischer, said on Tuesday he hoped recent interest rate cuts would lead to "a more accurate value" for the Australian dollar.

Asked on Reuters Financial Television about the impact of a strong Australian currency on exports, Fischer, who is also trade minister, said he was always concerned about any inaccuracies or "out of kilter dimension" to the local currency.

"We have had three official lowerings of interest rates in the last six months and that is setting a framework of a sustainably lower interest rate structure as we close up the budget deficit," he said. "That hopefully will engender a
setting of a more accurate value for the Australian dollar."
The Australian dollar is currently trading at about US$0.7783. It has traded as high as $0.8212 recently.
The Reserve Bank of Australia last reduced official interest rates by 50 basis points to 6.0 percent on December 11.
